argument_summary: Certification is supportable on the present admissible record only as caveated compliance: the current release passes aggregate readiness by 2.3 points, had no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and the prior approval can be used only as context because it predates the locale-routing update and current eval batch. The limiting fact is current and specific: the Spanish-language billing slice is 2.1 points below the warning threshold. Because no admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance or a reviewed mitigation for that subgroup regression, the defensible certification basis is that current release documentation must disclose the subgroup weakness and current evaluation results before launch.
claims_about_business_cost: Business-cost considerations do not change the policy standard. Remaining uncertainty can be handled without escalation if certification is treated as caveated and the required disclosure is made in the current release documentation.
claims_about_policy: The governing policy is not satisfied by the stale approval or the informal monitoring note standing alone. The policy permits certification if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and material segment weaknesses are disclosed, unless they are instead covered by approved mitigation. On this record, the clean supportable position is that certification remains within policy when tied to current model-card disclosure of the Spanish-language billing limitation; it is weaker and overbroad to argue that prior approval already covers this release.
concessions: The Spanish-language billing support slice is a material current limitation because it is 2.1 percentage points below the warning threshold.
The prior approval is contextual only and does not substitute for current evidence for this release.
The release thread's monitoring comment is supplemental context, not approved mitigation or risk acceptance.
An unconditional clean-compliance theory is not well supported by the admissible record.
